records.title: Energy-Efficient Collaborative DNN Inference in UAV Swarm
records.venue: 2023 9th International Conference on Big Data Computing and Communications (BIGCOM)

identity_evidence.quote: Energy-Efficient Collaborative DNN Inference in UAV Swarm

primary_full_report.rationale: Full 8-page IEEE BIGCOM 2023 conference paper presenting a system model, latency-minimization optimization formulation, online heuristic EECIA, and simulation evaluation.
primary_full_report.quote: In this paper, we propose a fine-grained DNN inference partition method, aiming at allocating inference requests to the resource-constrained UAV swarm, classifying the captured images, and finding the minimum inference latency.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Models a wireless ad hoc UAV swarm of I rotary-wing UAVs and evaluates 3 to 11 UAVs across AlexNet, ResNet152, and VGG-16 (Table II and Figs. 3-5).
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: Then we use three UAVs to collaboratively execute inference task of AlexNet, five UAVs to execute ResNet152 and VGG-16.

collaborative_inference.rationale: Partitions CNN layers and divides computationally heavy layers into subtasks executed in parallel across multiple UAVs, transmitting intermediate layer outputs within the swarm.
collaborative_inference.quote: Thus, we consider that the calculation of one layer can be divided into multiple subtasks and allocated to multiple UAVs for parallel calculation, so as to reduce the latency.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Conducts numerical simulations solving Eq. (10) on AlexNet, ResNet152, and VGG-16 parameterized by Raspberry Pi 3B+, Orange Pi Zero, and Odroid profiles against Random, Nearest, DistInference, and OPT.
evaluative_evidence.quote: We evaluate the performance of our system on three different CNN models throughout the simulation, including AlexNet, ResNet152 and VGG-16 [12].

date_window.rationale: Published in 2023 IEEE BIGCOM proceedings (2023 copyright), within 2021-01-01 through 2026-11-25.
date_window.quote: 2023 9th International Conference on Big Data Computing and Communications (BIGCOM)

english.rationale: Full 8-page conference paper is written in English.
english.quote: The large amount of data generated by these applications needs to be processed and analyzed by deep neural networks (DNNs).

alignment.quote: In this paper, we design a collaborative inference model system of UAV swarm, and classify the input images by deploying convolution neural networks (CNNs) in the UAV swarm.

records.title: Efficient Pipeline Collaborative DNN Inference in Resource-constrained UAV Swarm
records.venue: 2024 IEEE Wireless Communications and Networking Conference (WCNC)

identity_evidence.quote: Efficient Pipeline Collaborative DNN Inference in Resource-constrained UAV Swarm

primary_full_report.rationale: Full 6-page IEEE WCNC 2024 conference paper presenting a pipeline collaborative DNN inference model, problem formulation, action-disassembled DRL algorithm, and trace-driven simulation results.
primary_full_report.quote: In this paper, we study how to achieve fast DNN inference in UAV swarm by the collaboration of multiple UAVs, and formulate the problem of minimizing the completion time of a series of arriving DNN inference tasks, under memory and energy constraints.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Models an N-UAV pipeline swarm and evaluates 5 UAVs executing 10 to 80 arriving CNN inference tasks over practical UAV mobility traces.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: Fig. 3 presents some measurement results of our algorithm during the experiment involving the use of 5 UAVs to perform 10 VGG-16 inference tasks.

collaborative_inference.rationale: Partitions arriving CNN inference tasks across N UAV pipeline stages at split points so each UAV executes a dynamically adjusted subset of layers and passes intermediate outputs to the next UAV.
collaborative_inference.quote: In our application scenario, the number of DNN layers executed by each UAV for each task needs to dynamically change.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Evaluates AlexNet, GoogLeNet, and VGG-16 in trace-driven simulations using Mid-Air UAV trajectory traces against Random, Comm-Min, Cal-Avg, Layer-Avg, and CoDNN baselines.
evaluative_evidence.quote: We conduct extensive simulations on popular DNN models AlexNet, GoogLeNet, and VGG-16 to evaluate the performance of the proposed algorithm, based on practical UAV mobility traces.

records.title: Dynamic DNN Model Switching for Collaborative Edge Intelligence in UAV Swarm
records.venue: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)

identity_evidence.quote: Dynamic DNN Model Switching for Collaborative Edge Intelligence in UAV Swarm

primary_full_report.rationale: Full 7-page IEEE WCSP 2023 conference paper presenting a system model, accuracy-latency utility optimization, genetic-algorithm-based Dynamic Model Switching (DMS) algorithm, and trace-driven simulations.
primary_full_report.quote: Based on genetic algorithms, we then propose an efficient algorithm called Dynamic Model Switching (DMS) that can output the best DNN model switching policy according to the current UAV communication environment.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Models N heterogeneous UAVs with time-varying links and evaluates swarms of 4 to 8 UAVs (5 UAVs in Fig. 2 and Table 1) using real-world Mid-Air trajectory traces.
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: To provide a clearer comparison of the performance of the five algorithms, we have created Table. 1, which displays the latency and accuracy for a swarm of five UAVs under seven inference request scenario.

collaborative_inference.rationale: Dynamically switches each request between single-UAV execution of a lightweight CNN (AlexNet/SqueezeNet) and multi-UAV layer-partitioned execution of a large CNN (VGG16) across swarm UAVs.
collaborative_inference.quote: In collaborative inference, large complex model needs to be partitioned and executed on different UAVs.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Evaluates VGG16 paired with AlexNet and SqueezeNet in Mid-Air trace-driven simulations using embedded hardware parameters against GA-uniform, GA-random, Small-only, and Large-only baselines.
evaluative_evidence.quote: In our study, we employ VGG16 as the large complex model, while for the small lightweight model, we utilize both AlexNet and SqueezeNet.

date_window.rationale: Published in 2023 IEEE WCSP proceedings (2023 copyright), within 2021-01-01 through 2026-11-25.
date_window.quote: 2023 International Conference on Wireless Communications and Signal Processing (WCSP)

english.rationale: Full 7-page conference paper is written in English.
english.quote: Deploying machine learning (ML) algorithms on Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarm to perform real-time tasks such as object detection is currently a hot research topic.

records.primary_reason: All six gates YES: primary_full_report, multi_uav_evaluated, collaborative_inference, evaluative_evidence, date_window, english.

alignment.quote: By dynamically switching between these two models, we have developed an efficient DNN model execution policy that achieves both low latency and high accuracy.

records.title: Learning-Based UAV Swarm Video Analytics Orchestration in Disaster Response Management

identity_evidence.quote: Learning-Based UAV Swarm Video Analytics Orchestration in Disaster Response Management

primary_full_report.rationale: Full 24-page peer-reviewed Springer Nature SN Computer Science original research article (received 12 October 2024, accepted 15 May 2025, published online 09 June 2025).
primary_full_report.quote: In this paper, we propose a comprehensive orchestration framework that integrates both offline and online strategies to optimize UAV video transmission, multi-UAV networking, and network management.

multi_uav_evaluated.rationale: Simulates 10-30 drones in offline experiment settings (Table 2) and a 10-UAV swarm (7 search UAVs and 3 ferry UAVs) in the online Q-LADTR routing and trajectory experiments (Table 3, Figs. 7 and 11-12).
multi_uav_evaluated.quote: The UAV network environment is a 1x1 grid with 10 random UAVs placed in their own 0.2x0.2 sized cells. The GS is in the center of the 1x1 grid located at [0.5, 0.5].

collaborative_inference.rationale: Assessed separately per component: (1) Offline/trajectory-DQN component (SNCS.pdf pp. 6-13, 15 Table 2, 17, 19-21) includes real neural inference via YOLOv8 and evaluates three-way execution placement (local UAV, UAV-Edge-Server collaboration citing [49], or full edge-server offloading) plus video codec/resolution/bitrate/protocol selection and switching to a more powerful edge model on insufficient confidence, benchmarked on 320 FFmpeg clips on one Nvidia Jetson Xavier NX (p. 17) while Table 2 configures 10-30 drones with fleet sizes and swarm TCP video offloading (pp. 15, 17) and pp. 12-13 formulate a multi-agent DQN switching Analytics/System Layer policies; (2) Online Q-LADTR component (SNCS.pdf pp. 13-16, 18, 20-22) evaluates a 10-UAV swarm (7 search, 3 ferry) performing mobility and store-carry-forward packet forwarding/dropping (goodput, RTT, buffer status) with no DNN inference workload or offloading variable. Although absence of layer partitioning or inter-UAV DNN execution does not exclude Amendment 001 request/resource orchestration, the supplied text leaves unresolved whether the evaluated inference-offloading/DQN component orchestrates inference requests/resources across a multi-UAV-edge hierarchy or evaluates per-UAV single-drone-to-edge offloading separately from the 10-UAV Q-LADTR routing simulation (Fig. 3 p. 7; p. 2).
collaborative_inference.quote: The process is divided into offline and online phases, addressing both UAV-Edge-Server collaboration and multi-UAV collaboration, which together ensure efficient data collection, processing, and decision-making.

evaluative_evidence.rationale: Evaluates offline video-streaming policies across 320 FFmpeg clips processed with YOLOv8 on an Nvidia Jetson Xavier NX (1,280 streaming scenarios) and online DQN/Rainbow DQN trajectory-policy simulations against UAV-only, Batch RL, ARSB, and Oracle baselines (SNCS.pdf pp. 9-11, 17, 19-21), alongside a 100-episode Q-LADTR multi-UAV routing simulation (SNCS.pdf pp. 16, 18, 20-22).
evaluative_evidence.quote: These videos were then processed on a Nvidia Jetson Xavier NX using the YoloV8 model [48] to conduct real-time object detection, providing key confidence data and processing speed.

date_window.rationale: Published online 09 June 2025 in SN Computer Science (2025) 6:537, within 2021-01-01 through 2026-11-25.

english.rationale: Full 24-page journal article is written in English.
english.quote: However, unstable network conditions in disaster environments pose significant challenges to maintaining reliable video transmission and real-time decision-making.

records.primary_reason: collaborative_inference: Offline/trajectory-DQN experiments evaluate video-streaming policy selection and three-way local/collaborative/edge offloading with YOLOv8 benchmarking on a single Jetson Xavier NX (SNCS.pdf pp. 7, 9-13, 17, 19-21) alongside a 10-30 drone Table 2 configuration (p. 15), whereas the evaluated 10-UAV Q-LADTR experiment optimizes packet forwarding and mobility only (pp. 14, 18, 20-22), leaving multi-UAV-edge inference orchestration linkage under Amendment 001 unresolved.

alignment.rationale: Alignment cannot be finalized as core_orchestration or outside_scope because SNCS.pdf evaluates UAV-edge video-analytics offloading/model-choice policies with YOLOv8 on a Jetson Xavier NX within a 10-30 drone offline setup (pp. 7, 9, 15, 17, 19-21) separately from its 10-UAV Q-LADTR packet-routing simulation (pp. 14, 18, 20-22), leaving multi-UAV-edge inference orchestration unresolved.
alignment.quote: For network performance evaluation, we introduced a network offloading strategy for UAV swarms utilizing TCP video streaming, with streams limited by different bit rates (500kbs, 1 mbs, 2 mbs, 4 mbs), generating 1280 unique streaming scenarios.

unresolved: Unresolved whether the evaluated offline Policy/Batch-RL and online trajectory-DQN video-analytics experiments (SNCS.pdf pp. 7, 9-13, 15 Table 2, 17, 19-21) jointly orchestrate inference requests/resources across multiple UAVs and an edge server (as suggested by Table 2's 10-30 drones, p. 17's fleet-size and swarm TCP offloading description, and Fig. 6's multi-agent DQN) or evaluate per-UAV single-drone-to-edge offloading without cross-UAV coordination (as suggested by Fig. 3 p. 7 separating UAV-Edge-Server collaboration from Multi-UAV collaboration, p. 2 noting concurrent UAVs without direct communication, and p. 17 running YOLOv8 on a single Jetson Xavier NX).

Unspecified internal workload division inside the partial-assistance 'Collaboration' branch (SNCS.pdf p. 7 citing [49]; Fig. 4 p. 9): the text specifies video codec/resolution/bitrate/protocol selection and offloading to a more powerful edge model when confidence is insufficient (pp. 9, 17), without specifying layer/feature splitting or multi-node DNN execution mechanics.

No evaluated end-to-end linkage is reported connecting the 10-UAV Q-LADTR store-carry-forward routing simulation (SNCS.pdf pp. 13-16, 18, 20-22, Figs. 7, 10-12) to YOLOv8 detection accuracy, FPS, or inference offloading decisions.

Possible study-family/author-group link to prior works cited in references [9], [23], [43], [44], [51], and [57] (Qu et al. / Ballotti / Goins & Gao) on UAV video-analytics orchestration and DroneNet-Sim (SNCS.pdf pp. 23-24).

Reassessed SNCS pp. 6-10 and 17-20 separately from Q-LADTR (pp. 14, 18) under Amendment 001: absence of DNN layer splitting or inter-UAV DNN execution is not a valid exclusion, but the evaluated linkage between the YOLOv8/policy/DQN video-analytics offloading component and a multi-UAV-edge hierarchy remains unresolved, requiring collaborative_inference=UNCERTAIN, decision=UNCERTAIN, and alignment.category=uncertain; also clarified evaluative_evidence.rationale to distinguish Figs. 5 and 8-9 baselines from Q-LADTR Figs. 10-12.
correction_notes.inference_component: Evaluates three-way execution placement (local UAV, UAV-Edge-Server collaboration citing [49], or full edge-server offloading) plus video-streaming policy selection (H.264/H.265 codec, resolution, bitrate, transport/application protocol) driven by YOLOv8 object-detection confidence thresholds (above 70%, 60%-70%, below 60%) on 320 FFmpeg clips benchmarked on an Nvidia Jetson Xavier NX, including offloading to a more powerful edge-server model under insufficient confidence (SNCS.pdf pp. 6-7, 9-11, 17), alongside Batch RL and multi-agent DQN switching of Analytics Layer and System Layer policy factors and trajectories (SNCS.pdf pp. 10-13, 19-21).
correction_notes.multi_uav_linkage: Offline setup configures 10-30 drones in a hierarchical UAV-Edge-Server network considering mobility models, fleet sizes, and a TCP video-streaming offloading strategy for UAV swarms across 1,280 streaming scenarios (SNCS.pdf p. 15 Table 2, p. 17), and Fig. 6/pp. 12-13 formulate a multi-agent DQN evaluated in Figs. 8-9 (pp. 19-21). Separately, the online Q-LADTR experiment simulates 10 UAVs (7 search, 3 ferry) on a 1x1 grid optimizing mobility and store-carry-forward packet forwarding/dropping via buffer status, RTT, and goodput without DNN inference or offloading actions (SNCS.pdf pp. 13-16, 18, 20-22). The text does not report whether the 10-30 drone offline/DQN inference-offloading evaluations coordinate requests/resources across multiple UAVs or treat each UAV's video offloading independently, nor does it link Q-LADTR routing outputs to YOLOv8 accuracy/FPS.
correction_notes.contrary_evidence: Against inclusion: Fig. 3 separates UAV-Edge-Server collaboration from Multi-UAV collaboration (SNCS.pdf p. 7); p. 2 states multiple UAVs often operate concurrently without direct communication; p. 17 benchmarks YOLOv8 on a single Jetson Xavier NX; Q-LADTR (pp. 14, 18) is purely packet-routing/mobility control; and no layer partitioning, inter-UAV DNN execution, or fleet-size inference-allocation sensitivity plots appear in Figs. 5 or 8-12 (pp. 9-11, 19-21). Against exclusion: pp. 7 and 9-10 explicitly model and evaluate local/collaborative/edge task-distribution policies (`[49]`) using YOLOv8 accuracy/FPS; p. 17 offloads from Xavier NX to a more powerful edge model within a 10-30 drone offline setup (Table 2 p. 15) and swarm TCP offloading scenarios; and pp. 12-13, 19-21 evaluate multi-agent DQN policy-layer orchestration under Amendment 001 where layer splitting is not required.
correction_notes.eligibility_reasoning: Five gates (primary_full_report, multi_uav_evaluated, evaluative_evidence, date_window, english) pass YES (SNCS.pdf pp. 1, 17-18). collaborative_inference is UNCERTAIN because the paper evaluates real YOLOv8 inference placement/offloading and video-policy decisions (pp. 7, 9-13, 17, 19-21) alongside multi-UAV setups (Table 2 p. 15; Q-LADTR pp. 14, 18), yet neither establishes nor refutes multi-UAV-edge inference request/resource orchestration under Amendment 001. By the six-gate truth table, decision is UNCERTAIN and alignment.category is uncertain without venue-driven override.
